reviewer: root exact effective-design and primary-source review
reason: The declared ingredient-ratio endpoint does not distinguish the named models: both (a,b) and (ka,kb) have ratio a/b. Fixed absolute amounts do not imply changing ingredient ratios when product count changes. No named matched recipe/count/amount observations are supplied. This is a logical design defect plus an absent concrete observation, not an empirical rejection of proportional scaling.

design.contrast: ratio-preserving scaling versus fixed indexed amounts
design.countermodel: The same surface alternation could reflect editorial batch conventions, lexicalized forms, or analyst counting choices without either proposed semantic rule.
design.falsifier: A matched count change preserves absolute amounts while the source explicitly marks a scaled batch, or ratios vary without a batch/count change.
design.prediction: When product count changes within the same recipe template, ingredient ratios should remain constant under the scaling model; the indexed model predicts stable absolute amounts and changing ratios.
design.principal_risk: Independent product counts and ingredient amounts are unavailable. Near IDEA000049 quantity calibration and old recipe quantity families, but the contrast is transformation across batch size, not unit interpretation or conservation.
design.unit: matched recipe records with an explicit product count and at least two ingredient amounts

all_of.detail: Replace the ratio-only discriminator with a predeclared absolute-amount scaling factor or amount-per-product comparison using an actual product-count change and comparable independently read amounts. A known historical unit or ingredient name is unnecessary if comparability and scale are independently established. Preserve the original design in history; a new design must explicitly correct its rival prediction.

not_sufficient: Existing analyst operation/meaning labels reused as outcome observations.
More pages without the specified contrast or evasion of the old family scope gate.

claim_ceiling: No empirical meaning refutation or universal demand for named substances/full translation. Source-free proposals remain retrievable under submitted semantic scope.
